# Uniqueness of the Feller semigroup generated by the neutral Wright–Fisher operator on polynomials

Let $(Q_t)$ be a strongly continuous positive contraction semigroup on $C[0, 1]$ whose generator $B$ extends $(\mathcal{L}_0, \text{polynomials})$, with $\mathcal{L}_0 = \frac{1}{2} x(1 - x) \frac{d^2}{dx^2}$. Then $Q_t = P_t$, the neutral Wright–Fisher semigroup.

By [the necessity half of the Hille–Yosida theorem](../../../../Probability/markov-chains/markov-processes-from-transition-semigroups/necessity-half-of-hille-yosida-generators-of-con.md), $\lambda - B$ is injective for $\lambda > 0$ and $(\lambda - B)^{-1}$ is the Laplace transform of $(Q_t)$. Since $\lambda - \mathcal{L}_0$ has dense range on the polynomials, as [the polynomials form a core](polynomials-form-a-core-for-the-neutral-wf-semig.md), $B$ is the closure of $\mathcal{L}_0$. So the resolvents of $(Q_t)$ and $(P_t)$ coincide, and by uniqueness of the Laplace transform so do the semigroups. The sufficiency direction of the Hille–Yosida theorem is not used.

## Expansion

1. The identification $B = \overline{\mathcal{L}_0}$ from injectivity and the dense range.
2. Equality of resolvents, then of semigroups.
3. A check: applied to the limit semigroup of the Bernstein operators, it gives the identity map between the two constructions.

## Sources

- S. N. Ethier and T. G. Kurtz, *Markov Processes: Characterization and Convergence*, Wiley (1986), <https://doi.org/10.1002/9780470316658>, Chapter 1, Sections 2 and 3 (the Hille–Yosida theorem and cores).
